Subject: Auckland Campus only - Plagiarism workshop







Workshop Title:
Why merely policing plagiarism is not the answer: a workshop exploring
the plagiarism issue and looking at how to use assessment and effective
teaching strategies to reduce the incidence and opportunities for
plagiarism.  
 
This workshop will be conducted by Professor Ranald Macdonald from
Sheffield Hallam University.
 
At Wellington on Monday, 31 March  between 10.30 and 12.30,  Venue to be
arranged
 
At Palmerston North at Kura Awa on Tuesday, 1 April between 2 and 4pm
 
At Auckland Wednesday, 2 April between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m.    Venue to be
arranged

Enrolments to:   mailto:q.anpjb@massey.ac.nz 

This is an excellent opportunity to participate in a workshop led by
Professor Ranald Macdonald who has researched and written extensively on
this subject and has led many workshops addressing the plagiarism issue
in a number of countries.   
"Ranald Macdonald is Professor of Academic Development and Head of
Strategic Development in the Learning and Teaching Institute. His main
research and scholarly interests are in the areas of academic
development, assessment and plagiarism, and problem-based learning. As
Co-Director of Sheffield Hallam University's Centre for Promoting
Learner Autonomy he is also involved in developing a research and
evaluation strategy for the Centre for Excellence in Learning and
Teaching (CETL). He is Chair of the Staff and Educational Development
Association's (SEDA) Research Committee and convenor of the SEDA/SRHE
Educational Development Research Network. He is a previous Co-Chair of
SEDA and a Fellowship holder, Ranald convened the 2007 6th International
Conference of the International Consortium for Educational Development
(ICED)". Further information about Professor Macdonald is available from
his website at:
(http://www.shu.ac.uk/research/ern/sp_ranald_macdonald.html)
We are very fortunate to be able to host this workshop as Professor
Macdonald is in New Zealand only briefly as External Advisor to the
Teaching and Learning Research Initiative project involving all eight
New Zealand Universities: Unlocking Student Learning: The Impact of
Teaching and Learning Enhancement Initiatives on First Year University
Students (2006-2009), a project led by Massey University

Gordon Suddaby
Director
Academic Development and eLearning
